svg.title: QSSC-P0.2.0 assembly: per-CNC-layer top views rendered from gcode + cross-section
svg.desc: Top view of every CNC job rendered from the actual gcode toolpaths (Job A Ag cathode stencil, Job B serpentine TEOS+NV entanglement bus, Job C Au/Cr detector stencil on ITO glass, Job D FR4 carrier with 130 holes) plus the vertical assembly cross-section and the serial-bus entanglement explanation.
svg.text: QSSC-P0 . 2.0 assembly: every CNC layer rendered from the real gcode + cross-section

vertical 3-layer stack on one 20x20 die . L3 graphene/MoS2 detector on ITO glass TOP / L2 TEOS+NV entanglement bus MIDDLE / L1 CQD emitter on ITO glass BOTTOM . 4 CNC jobs, 1 mm bit . 64 NV sites wired in series on one bus
THE 4 CNC LAYERS (top view of each, drawn from the .gcode toolpaths at the centred die pocket (57.5,35))

g.text: Job A - L1 BOTTOM face: Ag cathode stencil (64)
the face that points DOWN to the carrier . Kapton stencil . drawn from p0_cathode_stencil.gcode
PURPOSE: cut a 64-window Kapton mask so Ag paste doctor-bladed through it forms 64 isolated cathode pads on L1's bottom face.
What the CNC does
- cut 64 square window openings through 50 um Kapton (Z-0.06)
- 8x8 grid, 2.5 mm pitch, window 1.0 mm (NOT 1.5)
- 1 mm bit + 1.0 mm window at 2.5 mm pitch -> 0.5 mm Kapton web
-> 64 isolated openings (at 1.5 mm the kerfs touch -> Ag shorts)
Then (not CNC)
doctor-blade Ag paste through the 64 windows onto the ZnO
-> 64 Ag cathode pads
L1 ITO is a CONTINUOUS common anode (no isolation grooves):
EM_ANODE = silver-epoxy on a bare-ITO corner (masked during
stack deposition); diode rectification stops pixel cross-talk
Materials
20x20x1.1 mm ITO-coated glass (150 nm ITO, continuous anode)
50 um Kapton foil (stencil) . Ag paste . silver epoxy (EM_ANODE)
1.0 mm flat end-mill . backing board . bond BEFORE seating
Job C - L3 TOP face: detector stencil (64 Au/Cr pads) on ITO glass
top of the stack . ITO glass + MoS2/graphene + Au/Cr pads . drawn from p0_detector_stencil.gcode
PURPOSE: cut a 64-window Kapton mask so Au/Cr doctor-bladed through it forms 64 graphene-detector readout pads, then spin PMMA passivation over the channels.
What the CNC does
- cut 64 Au/Cr pad openings through 50 um Kapton (Z-0.06), 8x8 grid,
2.5 mm pitch, window 1.0 mm (same 0.5 mm web limit as Job A)
- align Kapton over the L3 ITO glass via shared corner fiducials
Then (not CNC)
doctor-blade Au/Cr through the 64 windows -> 64 detector readout pads,
one per pixel, each reading the NV red PL (637-800 nm) from the
L2 site directly beneath it
spin PMMA passivation (F3.1b): keep the 64 Kapton cutout squares,
place one on each pad -> spin ~150 nm PMMA over the channels, peel
squares -> pads stay bare for bonding
Materials
L3 substrate = ITO glass (ITO film = detector common masa, DET_COMMON,
edge-contacted); PL enters through the glass face (transparent at 637-800 nm)
graphene-in-alcohol flake ink + MoS2-nanosheet ink (LPE from powder, F3.0),
spin-coat MoS2 first then graphene (vdW adhesion + PMMA edge-lock, no CVD)
50 um Kapton . Au/Cr paste . 1 mm bit . PMMA 950K (passivation + edge-lock)
bond 64 top contacts + DET_COMMON AFTER seating
Job D - FR4 carrier 135x90 (one die pocket + 130 holes)
breakout for the stacked die . 2 mm pin pitch . drawn from p0_carrier_pcb.gcode
PURPOSE: machine the FR4 holder (one die pocket + 130 bond holes + outline) that seats the stacked die and brings all 130 contacts to a 2 mm socket.
stacked die seats here
64 emitter-cathode holes (Y=5)
64 detector holes (Y=85)
EM_ANODE (3.5,8.0)
DET_COMMON (3.5,82.0)
What the CNC does
- pocket ONE 20x20 x 1.1 mm die cavity at (57.5,35) [raster fill shown]
- peck-drill 130 Ø1 holes through FR4 at 2 mm pitch:
64 emitter-cathode (Y=5) + 64 detector (Y=85)
+ 1 EM_ANODE (3.5,8.0) + 1 DET_COMMON (3.5,82.0) = the 2 ITO commons
- through-cut the 135x90 outline with 4 bridges (Z-3.0)
-> 2 mm male pin headers -> Samtec/Harwin 2 mm socket
ASSEMBLY ORDER (4 CNC jobs, 1 mm bit, no tool change)
vertical 3-layer stack on one 20x20 two-faced die . no TSV . 130 bond holes
Job A - L1 BOTTOM: Ag cathode stencil (64 windows)
Kapton mask, doctor-blade Ag -> 64 cathode pads on the L1 bottom face.
L1 ITO is a CONTINUOUS common anode (no isolation grooves): EM_ANODE =
silver-epoxy on a bare-ITO corner (masked during stack deposition);
diode rectification stops pixel cross-talk.
Job B - L2 TOP: serpentine entanglement bus (64 NV sites in series)
One continuous boustrophedon core threads all 64 NV microdiamonds on
one TEOS-sol-gel optical core -> the on-chip entanglement bus.
Job C - L3 TOP: Au/Cr detector stencil (64 pads) on ITO glass
L3 substrate = ITO glass; the ITO film is the detector common masa
(DET_COMMON, edge-contacted). Spin-coat MoS2-ink + graphene-in-alcohol,
64 Au/Cr readout pads, PMMA passivation over the channels.
Job D - FR4 carrier 135x90 (one die pocket + 130 holes)
64 detector (Y=85) + 64 emitter-cathode (Y=5) + EM_ANODE (3.5,8.0) +
DET_COMMON (3.5,82.0) = 130 bond holes -> 2 mm socket on a breakout.
Bond the 64 bottom cathodes + EM_ANODE BEFORE seating the die;
seat, then bond the 64 top detector contacts + DET_COMMON.
532 nm pump in at the L2 LEFT facet -> walks the serial bus -> every NV
site pumped in sequence -> red PL (637-800 nm) UP to the L3 graphene pad
above each site -> lock-in readout at the 2.87 GHz ODMR dip.
ASSEMBLY cross-section (vertical stack, top -> bottom)
thickness exaggerated . die clamped between two contact planes . 532 pump from LEFT . PL up . no TSV
2 mm pin row . top edge Y=85 . 64 detector bonds + DET_COMMON
64 detector contacts (Au/Cr, TOP)
L3 . ITO glass + graphene/MoS2 photodetector + PMMA
ITO film = DET_COMMON masa (edge-contacted)
L2 . TEOS sol-gel ENTANGLEMENT BUS + 64 NV sites
serpentine core, 64 NV
sites in series

L1 . CQD emitter 8x8 (green LED)

ZnO/Ag (see Job A)
ITO = continuous EM_ANODE (edge)
64 Ag cathodes + EM_ANODE (BOTTOM)
FR4 carrier 1.6 mm (one 20x20 die pocket)
2 mm pin row . bottom edge Y=5 . 64 cathode bonds + EM_ANODE
bond bottom cathodes + EM_ANODE BEFORE seating the die

two-faced die . 20x20 . no TSV
Stack order + physics
1. Job A: 64 Ag cathodes on L1 bottom (Kapton stencil). L1 ITO = CONTINUOUS common anode (EM_ANODE =
silver-epoxy on a bare-ITO corner, masked during stack deposition; no isolation grooves). Spin PEDOT/TFB/CQD-PVA/ZnO.
2. Job B: mill the serpentine entanglement bus on L2; fill with TEOS + NV microdiamonds; seat Cu MW loop.
3. L3: LPE MoS2 powder -> ink (F3.0); clean ITO glass, spin-coat MoS2 + graphene-in-alcohol inks (ITO film = DET_COMMON masa);
Job C (64 Au/Cr pads); spin PMMA passivation (F3.1b). PL enters through the ITO glass face.
4. Job D: FR4 carrier (one die pocket + 130 holes). Stack L1+L2+L3 (index-matching epoxy; LEFT facet of L2 exposed for 532 pump); seat.
5. Bond 64 top detector contacts + DET_COMMON; 130 pins -> 2 mm socket on a breakout motherboard.
Readout: NV PL up the bus -> L3 graphene (lock-in, MW 2.87 GHz ODMR). Sole detector = graphene/MoS2 on ITO glass.
Materials + the serial entanglement bus
L1 emitter (bottom layer)
20x20x1.1 mm ITO glass (150 nm ITO, CONTINUOUS common anode) . PEDOT:PSS . TFB (chlorobenzene)
green Cd-free CQD-PVA . ZnO nanopowder . Ag paste (64 cathodes) . silver epoxy (EM_ANODE) . Kapton 50 um
L2 host layer (middle)
20x20x1 mm borosilicate glass . Ti-doped TEOS sol (n~1.55)
NV- microdiamonds 150-200 um (Adamas FMDNVLN, T1~5.9-10.2 ms) . Cu wire (MW loop)
L3 detector (top layer)
graphene-in-alcohol + MoS2-ink (LPE from powder) spin-coated on ITO glass (ITO film = DET_COMMON masa,
edge-contacted; PL enters through the glass face) . vdW adhesion + PMMA edge-lock . Kapton 50 um
PMMA 950K spin-coated passivation over the channels (F3.1b, pad-masked) . 1.0 mm flat end-mill (all 4 jobs, no tool change)
Carrier + pump
135x90x1.6 mm FR4 . 2 mm male pin headers . Samtec TMM-1xx / Harwin M20-782
2 mm female socket . 532 nm DPSS laser (left-facet pump) . magnet wire fan-out
The serial entanglement bus
One continuous boustrophedon core (8 runs + 7 connectors) threads all
64 NV microdiamonds IN SERIES on the same TEOS-sol-gel optical core.
532 nm pump enters the LEFT facet, walks the whole bus and pumps every
site in sequence. Each site's red PL (637-800 nm) leaves UP through the
wafer to the L3 graphene pad directly above it. Because all 64 sites share
one core, a photon from any site reaches any other -> two indistinguishable
photons interfere at the bus output -> spin-spin entanglement heralded. A Cu
loop in the perimeter groove baths all 64 sites at 2.87 GHz (ODMR); a
lock-in reads per-pixel detector photocurrent.
The 4 job panels above are rendered straight from the .gcode toolpaths
(tools/render_p0_svg.py) -> the drawings are the real cut geometry.
